set.body:
Defect: D7 (capability is implicit; nothing declares what a corpus has, so 'can this corpus run this arm' is answered by archaeology). But revision 2's version of this slice WAS THE D1 PATTERN RE-CREATED -- a declared record wired to nothing, which is the defect this whole epic exists to close.

Do: Capability DERIVED from OpenCorpus (a gold table at level L with n coders => PerUnitGold(L, n, coverage)), with the manifest's DECLARED set checked against it and refused on mismatch. Revision 1 let a manifest assert its own capabilities and a registry admit on that assertion -- identity asserted by the caller. Option[Double] fields that conflate unknown with absent become typed (Measured(d) | Unmeasured), on ImportanceWeight.unmeasured's precedent.

THE CONDITION ON THIS BEAD: it only earns its place if something CONSUMES the capability. The consumer is the P6 descriptor -- it carries the derived fields (gold level, coder count, recall grid, clock) and run-arm.sh / run-filmfestival.py refuse an arm whose declared needs are unmet. IF THAT CONSUMER IS NOT BUILT, DEFER THIS BEAD ENTIRELY, INCLUDING THE Capability ENUM.

Deferred either way, until a second experiment arm actually declares a requirement: CorpusRegistry, Requirement, CapabilityShape. `satisfying` has no caller today, and revision 1 used CapabilityShape without ever defining it.

Note: this slice CHANGES P2b-ii's contract -- it adds a new IntakeRefusal case inside open.

Exit: either a derived, checked, consumed capability set, or a recorded deferral.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S2 'Capabilities'; S3 P7
set.title: intake P7: capabilities derived from OpenCorpus AND consumed, or deferred entirely
